statements: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "ledger" ("account" text, "amount" bigint, "memo" text, "posted" date, PRIMARY KEY ("posted", "account"))
why: PRIMARY KEY in the physical order the layout gives, not the declared one. The key is still the model's - the same two columns, so the same uniqueness and the same `get` - and only which prefix the index can seek by has moved.

statements: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `reading` (`at` DateTime64(6, 'UTC'), `humidity` Int32, `station` String, `temperature` Float64) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree ORDER BY (`at`, `station`)
why: ORDER BY in the physical order the layout gives. In ClickHouse the key order decides which prefixes prune granules; `ReplacingMergeTree` deduplicates on the whole ORDER BY tuple, which is the same set of columns in either order, so the rows are the same rows.
